The FY2026 MILCON-VA bill's $152B discretionary allocation—$5B over last year—raises serious questions. While fully funding veterans' healthcare is non-negotiable, the unchecked 3% increase reeks of DC’s "spend first, audit never" approach. The bill claims to modernize military infrastructure but includes $1.8B for Indo-Pacific construction projects—code for open-ended foreign spending while veteran homelessness still plagues 33K+ Americans.

The Bridging Rental Assistance program sounds noble until you realize VA’s own 2024 audit found 14% of housing funds misallocated through contractor overbilling. Where’s the accountability mandate? The committee brags about rejecting amendments targeting DEI bloat but stays silent on why 28% of VA’s $343M rural health budget last year went to administrative overhead rather than direct care.

Real support means auditing every dollar, not rubber-stamping blanket increases. Until Congress ties funding to measurable outcomes—like reducing VA claim backlogs below 200K or cutting veteran suicide rates—these bills just fuel bureaucracy, not results.

This departure led to a loss of $594 million in potential wealth tax revenue, significantly undermining the policy's intended fiscal outcome. The phenomenon has been described as an unprecedented capital flight, with many high-net-worth Norwegians relocating to more tax-friendly jurisdictions such as Switzerland.
